subject: english-language
title: Dominance and Difference
welcome_lead: Zimmerman and West weigh interruptions; Tannen frames cross-cultural difference. Two heavyweight models.
meta_desc: Zimmerman & West dominance model and Tannen's difference model at A-Level English Language.
final_note: You have weighed dominance against difference — and seen why both need updating.

concepts.def: Approach (Zimmerman & West 1975) that mixed-sex talk reflects male dominance, evidenced by male interruptions.
Recorded 31 conversations on a US campus; 96% of interruptions in mixed-sex pairs came from men.
Deborah Tannen's framework (You Just Don't Understand, 1990) — men and women belong to different sub-cultures and miscommunicate.
Status vs support, advice vs understanding, independence vs intimacy, orders vs proposals, conflict vs compromise, information vs feelings.
Tannen contrasts women's rapport talk (relational) with men's report talk (informational).
Critics (Cameron) argue the difference model recycles stereotypes and ignores power.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Zimmerman and West recorded student conversations. In same-sex pairs interruptions were balanced; in mixed-sex pairs they were not.

96% of overlaps that violated current speaker rights came from male participants — evidence, they argued, of conversational dominance.

Tannen reframed mismatches as cross-cultural. Women use rapport talk to build connection; men use report talk to negotiate status.

Her six contrasts (status vs support, etc.) made her work hugely popular but also flattened individual variation.
Cameron and others point out that difference can obscure power. The same behaviour read as men's directness often hides asymmetric authority — a point dominance theorists never abandoned.

options: Women always use more hedges and tag questions than men.
Early studies (Lakoff) made broad claims, but later research (e.g. Holmes, Cameron) shows context matters more than gender, and many supposed differences disappear with proper data.

mcqs.q: What did Chomsky propose about language acquisition?
options: Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
Chomsky said children learn language entirely by copying adults.
Children possess an innate Language Acquisition Device — an inborn capacity for grammar — because exposure alone cannot account for how rapidly and uniformly children learn complex syntax.

mcqs.q: What is Skinner's behaviourist view of language acquisition?
options: Children learn language through imitation and operant conditioning — they are reinforced for correct utterances and corrected for errors.
Skinner believed in an innate grammar module.

Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
